verses.original: וַיְהִי֙ הָהֵ֔ם בַּיָּמִ֣ים אֵ֣ין וּמֶ֖לֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְהִ֣י׀ אִ֣ישׁ לֵוִ֗י גָּ֚ר בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֣י הַר־ אֶפְרַ֔יִם וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ לוֹ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה פִילֶ֔גֶשׁ מִבֵּ֥ית לֶ֖חֶם יְהוּדָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî hā·hêm bay·yā·mîm ’ên ū·me·leḵ bə·yiś·rā·’êl way·hî ’îš lê·wî gār bə·yar·kə·ṯê har- ’ep̄·ra·yim way·yiq·qaḥ- lōw ’iš·šāh p̄î·le·ḡeš mib·bêṯ le·ḥem yə·hū·ḏāh
verses.literal: Now in those days when there was no king in Israel . . . . . . a Levite who lived in the remote hill country of Ephraim took for himself vvv a concubine vvv from Bethlehem in Judah

verses.original: פִּֽילַגְשׁ֔וֹ וַתִּזְנֶ֤ה עָלָיו֙ וַתֵּ֤לֶךְ מֵֽאִתּוֹ֙ אֶל־ אָבִ֔יהָ בֵּ֣ית אֶל־ בֵּ֥ית לֶ֖חֶם יְהוּדָ֑ה וַתְּהִי־ שָׁ֕ם יָמִ֖ים אַרְבָּעָ֥ה חֳדָשִֽׁים׃
verses.transliteration: pî·laḡ·šōw wat·tiz·neh ‘ā·lāw wat·tê·leḵ mê·’it·tōw ’el- ’ā·ḇî·hā bêṯ ’el- bêṯ le·ḥem yə·hū·ḏāh wat·tə·hî- šām yā·mîm ’ar·bā·‘āh ḥo·ḏā·šîm
verses.literal: But she was unfaithful to him and left him to return to her father’s house in vvv Bethlehem in Judah After she had been there - four months

verses.original: אִישָׁ֜הּ וַיָּ֨קָם וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ אַחֲרֶ֗יהָ לְדַבֵּ֤ר לִבָּהּ֙ עַל־ לַהֲשִׁיבוֹ וְנַעֲר֥וֹ עִמּ֖וֹ וְצֶ֣מֶד חֲמֹרִ֑ים וַתְּבִיאֵ֙הוּ֙ אָבִ֔יהָ בֵּ֣ית הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ה אֲבִ֣י וַיִּרְאֵ֙הוּ֙ וַיִּשְׂמַ֖ח לִקְרָאתֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: ’î·šāh way·yā·qām way·yê·leḵ ’a·ḥă·re·hā lə·ḏab·bêr lib·bāh ‘al- la·hă·šī·ḇō wə·na·‘ă·rōw ‘im·mōw wə·ṣe·meḏ ḥă·mō·rîm wat·tə·ḇî·’ê·hū ’ā·ḇî·hā bêṯ han·na·‘ă·rāh ’ă·ḇî way·yir·’ê·hū way·yiś·maḥ liq·rā·ṯōw
verses.literal: her husband got up and went after her to speak kindly to her and bring her back taking his servant . . . and a pair of donkeys So [the girl] brought him into her father’s house and when [her] father saw him he gladly welcomed him

verses.original: חֹֽתְנוֹ֙ הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ה אֲבִ֣י וַיֶּחֱזַק־ בּ֤וֹ וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב אִתּ֖וֹ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וַיֹּאכְלוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁתּ֔וּ וַיָּלִ֖ינוּ שָֽׁם׃
verses.transliteration: ḥō·ṯə·nōw han·na·‘ă·rāh ’ă·ḇî way·ye·ḥĕ·zaq- bōw way·yê·šeḇ ’it·tōw šə·lō·šeṯ yā·mîm way·yō·ḵə·lū way·yiš·tū way·yā·lî·nū šām
verses.literal: His father-in-law the girl’s father persuaded him to stay . . . so he remained with him three days eating drinking and lodging there

verses.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ הָרְבִיעִ֔י בַּיּ֣וֹם וַיַּשְׁכִּ֥ימוּ בַבֹּ֖קֶר וַיָּ֣קָם לָלֶ֑כֶת הַֽנַּעֲרָ֜ה אֲבִ֨י וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֶל־ חֲתָנ֗וֹ סְעָ֧ד לִבְּךָ֛ פַּת־ לֶ֖חֶם וְאַחַ֥ר תֵּלֵֽכוּ׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî hā·rə·ḇî·‘î bay·yō·wm way·yaš·kî·mū ḇab·bō·qer way·yā·qām lā·le·ḵeṯ han·na·‘ă·rāh ’ă·ḇî way·yō·mer ’el- ḥă·ṯā·nōw sə·‘āḏ lib·bə·ḵā paṯ- le·ḥem wə·’a·ḥar tê·lê·ḵū
verses.literal: - On the fourth day they got up early in the morning and prepared to depart but the girl’s father said to his son-in-law Refresh your heart with a morsel of bread and then you can go

verses.original: וַיֵּשְׁב֗וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם וַיֹּאכְל֧וּ וַיִּשְׁתּ֑וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו הַֽנַּעֲרָה֙ אֲבִ֤י וַיֹּ֜אמֶר אֶל־ הָאִ֔ישׁ נָ֥א הֽוֹאֶל־ וְלִ֖ין לִבֶּֽךָ׃ וְיִטַ֥ב
verses.transliteration: way·yê·šə·ḇū šə·nê·hem way·yō·ḵə·lū way·yiš·tū yaḥ·dāw han·na·‘ă·rāh ’ă·ḇî way·yō·mer ’el- hā·’îš nā hō·w·’el- wə·lîn lib·be·ḵā wə·yi·ṭaḇ
verses.literal: So they sat down and the two of them ate and drank together Then the girl’s father said to the man Please agree to stay overnight and let your heart be merry

verses.original: הָאִ֖ישׁ וַיָּ֥קָם לָלֶ֑כֶת חֹתְנ֔וֹ וַיָּ֖שָׁב וַיִּפְצַר־ בּוֹ֙ וַיָּ֥לֶן שָֽׁם׃
verses.transliteration: hā·’îš way·yā·qām lā·le·ḵeṯ ḥō·ṯə·nōw way·yā·šāḇ way·yip̄·ṣar- bōw way·yā·len šām
verses.literal: The man got up to depart but his father-in-law . . . persuaded him so he stayed there that night

verses.original: הַחֲמִישִׁי֮ בַּיּ֣וֹם וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם בַּבֹּ֜קֶר לָלֶכֶת֒ הַֽנַּעֲרָ֗ה אֲבִ֣י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ נָא֙ סְעָד־ לְבָ֣בְךָ֔ וְהִֽתְמַהְמְה֖וּ עַד־ נְט֣וֹת הַיּ֑וֹם שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃ וַיֹּאכְל֖וּ
verses.transliteration: ha·ḥă·mî·šî bay·yō·wm way·yaš·kêm bab·bō·qer lā·le·ḵeṯ han·na·‘ă·rāh ’ă·ḇî way·yō·mer nā sə·‘āḏ- lə·ḇā·ḇə·ḵā wə·hiṯ·mah·mə·hū ‘aḏ- nə·ṭō·wṯ hay·yō·wm šə·nê·hem way·yō·ḵə·lū
verses.literal: On the fifth day he got up early in the morning to depart but the girl’s father said Please refresh your heart So they waited until late afternoon . . . and the two of them ate

verses.original: הָאִישׁ֙ וַיָּ֤קָם לָלֶ֔כֶת ה֥וּא וּפִילַגְשׁ֖וֹ וְנַעֲר֑וֹ חֹתְנ֣וֹ הַֽנַּעֲרָ֡ה אֲבִ֣י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֣וֹ הִנֵּ֣ה הַיּ֜וֹם רָפָ֨ה לַעֲרֹ֗ב נָא֩ לִֽינוּ־ נָ֞א הִנֵּ֨ה הַיּוֹם֙ חֲנ֤וֹת לִ֥ין פֹּה֙ לְבָבֶ֔ךָ וְיִיטַ֣ב וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּ֤ם מָחָר֙ לְדַרְכְּכֶ֔ם וְהָלַכְתָּ֖ לְאֹהָלֶֽךָ׃
verses.transliteration: hā·’îš way·yā·qām lā·le·ḵeṯ hū ū·p̄î·laḡ·šōw wə·na·‘ă·rōw ḥō·ṯə·nōw han·na·‘ă·rāh ’ă·ḇî way·yō·mer lōw hin·nêh hay·yō·wm rā·p̄āh la·‘ă·rōḇ nā lî·nū- nā hin·nêh hay·yō·wm ḥă·nō·wṯ lîn pōh lə·ḇā·ḇe·ḵā wə·yî·ṭaḇ wə·hiš·kam·tem mā·ḥār lə·ḏar·kə·ḵem wə·hā·laḵ·tā lə·’ō·hā·le·ḵā
verses.literal: When the man got up to depart . . . with his concubine and his servant his father-in-law the girl’s father said to him Look the day is drawing to a close Please spend the night . . . See the day is almost over Spend the night here that your heart may be merry Then you can get up early tomorrow for your journey . . . home

verses.original: הָאִישׁ֙ וְלֹֽא־ אָבָ֤ה לָל֔וּן וַיָּ֣קָם וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ וַיָּבֹא֙ עַד־ נֹ֣כַח יְב֔וּס הִ֖יא יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְעִמּ֗וֹ צֶ֤מֶד חֲבוּשִׁ֔ים חֲמוֹרִים֙ וּפִילַגְשׁ֖וֹ עִמּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: hā·’îš wə·lō- ’ā·ḇāh lā·lūn way·yā·qām way·yê·leḵ way·yā·ḇō ‘aḏ- nō·ḵaḥ yə·ḇūs hî yə·rū·šā·lim wə·‘im·mōw ṣe·meḏ ḥă·ḇū·šîm ḥă·mō·w·rîm ū·p̄î·laḡ·šōw ‘im·mōw
verses.literal: But the man was unwilling . . . to spend the night He got up and departed and arrived . . . opposite Jebus (that is Jerusalem) with his two saddled donkeys and his concubine -

verses.original: הֵ֣ם עִם־ יְב֔וּס וְהַיּ֖וֹם מְאֹ֑ד רַ֣ד הַנַּ֜עַר וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֶל־ אֲדֹנָ֗יו לְכָה־ נָּ֛א וְנָס֛וּרָה אֶל־ הַזֹּ֖את הַיְבוּסִ֥י עִֽיר־ וְנָלִ֥ין בָּֽהּ׃
verses.transliteration: hêm ‘im- yə·ḇūs wə·hay·yō·wm mə·’ōḏ raḏ han·na·‘ar way·yō·mer ’el- ’ă·ḏō·nāw lə·ḵāh- nā wə·nā·sū·rāh ’el- haz·zōṯ hay·ḇū·sî ‘îr- wə·nā·lîn bāh
verses.literal: When they were near Jebus and the day was almost gone the servant said to his master . . . Please let us stop at this Jebusite city and spend the night here

verses.original: אֲדֹנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ לֹ֤א נָסוּר֙ אֶל־ עִ֣יר נָכְרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־ מִבְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵ֑נָּה וְעָבַ֖רְנוּ עַד־ גִּבְעָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: ’ă·ḏō·nāw way·yō·mer ’ê·lāw lō nā·sūr ’el- ‘îr nā·ḵə·rî ’ă·šer lō- mib·bə·nê yiś·rā·’êl hên·nāh wə·‘ā·ḇar·nū ‘aḏ- giḇ·‘āh
verses.literal: But his master replied - We will not turn aside to the city of foreigners where there are no Israelites . . . . . . We will go on to Gibeah

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְנַעֲר֔וֹ לְךָ֥ וְנִקְרְבָ֖ה בְּאַחַ֣ד הַמְּקֹמ֑וֹת וְלַ֥נּוּ בַגִּבְעָ֖ה א֥וֹ בָרָמָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lə·na·‘ă·rōw lə·ḵå̄ wə·niq·rə·ḇāh bə·’a·ḥaḏ ham·mə·qō·mō·wṯ wə·lan·nū ḇag·giḇ·‘āh ’ōw ḇā·rā·māh
verses.literal: He continued - Come let us try to reach one of these towns to spend the night in Gibeah or Ramah

verses.original: וַיֵּלֵ֑כוּ וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ וַתָּבֹ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵ֥צֶל הַגִּבְעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְבִנְיָמִֽן׃
verses.transliteration: way·yê·lê·ḵū way·ya·‘aḇ·rū haš·še·meš wat·tā·ḇō lā·hem ’ê·ṣel hag·giḇ·‘āh ’ă·šer lə·ḇin·yā·min
verses.literal: So they continued on their journey and the sun set as they neared Gibeah - in Benjamin

verses.original: וַיָּסֻ֣רוּ שָׁ֔ם לָב֖וֹא לָל֣וּן בַּגִּבְעָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֗א וַיֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ הָעִ֔יר בִּרְח֣וֹב וְאֵ֥ין אִ֛ישׁ מְאַסֵּֽף־ אוֹתָ֥ם הַבַּ֖יְתָה לָלֽוּן׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·su·rū šām lā·ḇō·w lā·lūn bag·giḇ·‘āh way·yā·ḇō way·yê·šeḇ hā·‘îr bir·ḥō·wḇ wə·’ên ’îš mə·’as·sêp̄- ’ō·w·ṯām hab·bay·ṯāh lā·lūn
verses.literal: They stopped . . . to go in and lodge in Gibeah The Levite went in and sat down in the city square but no one would take them into his home for the night

verses.original: וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀ בָּעֶ֔רֶב זָקֵ֗ן אִ֣ישׁ וְהָאִישׁ֙ מֵהַ֣ר אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְהוּא־ גָ֖ר בַּגִּבְעָ֑ה וְאַנְשֵׁ֥י הַמָּק֖וֹם בְּנֵ֥י יְמִינִֽי׃ בָּ֣א מִֽן־ מַעֲשֵׂ֤הוּ מִן־ הַשָּׂדֶה֙
verses.transliteration: wə·hin·nêh bā·‘e·reḇ zā·qên ’îš wə·hā·’îš mê·har ’ep̄·ra·yim wə·hū- ḡār bag·giḇ·‘āh wə·’an·šê ham·mā·qō·wm bə·nê yə·mî·nî bā min- ma·‘ă·śê·hū min- haś·śā·ḏeh
verses.literal: - That evening an old man - from the hill country of Ephraim . . . who was residing in Gibeah the men of that place vvv were Benjamites came in from his work in the field

verses.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֣א עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּ֛רְא אֶת־ הָאִ֥ישׁ הָאֹרֵ֖חַ הָעִ֑יר בִּרְחֹ֣ב הַזָּקֵ֛ן הָאִ֧ישׁ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אָ֥נָה תֵלֵ֖ךְ וּמֵאַ֥יִן תָּבֽוֹא׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiś·śā ‘ê·nāw way·yar ’eṯ- hā·’îš hā·’ō·rê·aḥ hā·‘îr bir·ḥōḇ haz·zā·qên hå̄·ʾīš way·yō·mer ’ā·nāh ṯê·lêḵ ū·mê·’a·yin tā·ḇō·w
verses.literal: When he looked up . . . and saw - vvv the traveler in the city square the old man asked Where are you going and where have you come from

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אֲנַ֜חְנוּ עֹבְרִ֨ים מִבֵּֽית־ לֶ֣חֶם יְהוּדָה֮ עַד־ יַרְכְּתֵ֣י הַר־ אֶפְרַיִם֒ מִשָּׁ֣ם אָנֹ֔כִי וָאֵלֵ֕ךְ עַד־ בֵּ֥ית לֶ֖חֶם יְהוּדָ֑ה וְאֶת־ אֲנִ֣י הֹלֵ֔ךְ בֵּ֤ית יְהוָה֙ וְאֵ֣ין אִ֔ישׁ מְאַסֵּ֥ף אוֹתִ֖י הַבָּֽיְתָה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ê·lāw ’ă·naḥ·nū ‘ō·ḇə·rîm mib·bêṯ- le·ḥem yə·hū·ḏāh ‘aḏ- yar·kə·ṯê har- ’ep̄·ra·yim miš·šām ’ā·nō·ḵî wā·’ê·lêḵ ‘aḏ- bêṯ le·ḥem yə·hū·ḏāh wə·’eṯ- ’ă·nî hō·lêḵ bêṯ Yah·weh wə·’ên ’îš mə·’as·sêp̄ ’ō·w·ṯî hab·bā·yə·ṯāh
verses.literal: [The Levite] replied . . . We are traveling vvv from Bethlehem in Judah to the remote hill country of Ephraim where I am from I went to vvv Bethlehem in Judah - and now I am going to the house of the LORD but no one has taken me into his home

verses.original: יֵ֣שׁ וְגַם־ תֶּ֤בֶן גַּם־ מִסְפּוֹא֙ לַחֲמוֹרֵ֔ינוּ וְ֠גַם לֶ֣חֶם וָיַ֤יִן יֶשׁ־ לִי֙ וְלַֽאֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וְלַנַּ֖עַר עִם־ אֵ֥ין עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ כָּל־ דָּבָֽר׃ מַחְס֖וֹר
verses.transliteration: yêš wə·ḡam- te·ḇen gam- mis·pō·w la·ḥă·mō·w·rê·nū wə·ḡam le·ḥem wā·ya·yin yeš- lî wə·la·’ă·mā·ṯe·ḵā wə·lan·na·‘ar ‘im- ’ên ‘ă·ḇā·ḏe·ḵā kāl- dā·ḇār maḥ·sō·wr
verses.literal: even though there is both straw and feed for our donkeys and bread and wine . . . for me and the maidservant and young man with me There is nothing that we, your servants . . . . . . lack

verses.original: שָׁל֣וֹם לָ֔ךְ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַזָּקֵן֙ הָאִ֤ישׁ עָלָ֑י רַ֥ק כָּל־ מַחְסוֹרְךָ֖ רַ֥ק אַל־ תָּלַֽן׃ בָּרְח֖וֹב
verses.transliteration: šā·lō·wm lāḵ way·yō·mer haz·zā·qên hā·’îš ‘ā·lāy raq kāl- maḥ·sō·wr·ḵā raq ’al- tā·lan bā·rə·ḥō·wḇ
verses.literal: Peace to you said the old man Let me supply . . . everything you need Only do not spend the night in the square

verses.original: וַיְבִיאֵ֣הוּ לְבֵית֔וֹ וַיָּ֖בָול לַחֲמוֹרִ֑ים וַֽיִּרְחֲצוּ֙ רַגְלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּאכְל֖וּ וַיִּשְׁתּֽוּ׃
verses.transliteration: way·ḇî·’ê·hū lə·ḇê·ṯōw way·yå̄·ḇå̄·wl la·ḥă·mō·w·rîm way·yir·ḥă·ṣū raḡ·lê·hem way·yō·ḵə·lū way·yiš·tū
verses.literal: So he brought him to his house and fed his donkeys And they washed their feet and ate and drank

verses.original: הֵמָּה֮ מֵיטִיבִ֣ים אֶת־ לִבָּם֒ וְהִנֵּה֩ בְלִיַּ֗עַל אַנְשֵׁ֨י הָעִ֜יר אַנְשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי־ נָסַ֙בּוּ֙ אֶת־ הַבַּ֔יִת מִֽתְדַּפְּקִ֖ים עַל־ הַדָּ֑לֶת וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אֶל־ הַזָּקֵן֙ הָ֠אִישׁ בַּ֣עַל הַבַּ֤יִת לֵאמֹ֔ר הוֹצֵ֗א אֶת־ הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֥א אֶל־ בֵּיתְךָ֖ וְנֵדָעֶֽנּוּ׃
verses.transliteration: hêm·māh mê·ṭî·ḇîm ’eṯ- lib·bām wə·hin·nêh ḇə·lî·ya·‘al ’an·šê hā·‘îr ’an·šê ḇə·nê- nā·sab·bū ’eṯ- hab·ba·yiṯ miṯ·dap·pə·qîm ‘al- had·dā·leṯ way·yō·mə·rū ’el- haz·zā·qên hā·’îš ba·‘al hab·ba·yiṯ lê·mōr hō·w·ṣê ’eṯ- hā·’îš ’ă·šer- bā ’el- bê·ṯə·ḵā wə·nê·ḏā·‘en·nū
verses.literal: While they were enjoying - themselves suddenly the wicked men of the city - - surrounded - the house Pounding on the door they said to the old man who owned the house - Bring out - the man who came to your house so we can have relations with him

verses.original: הָאִישׁ֙ בַּ֣עַל הַבַּ֔יִת וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַל־ אַחַ֖י אַל־ תָּרֵ֣עוּ נָ֑א אַ֠חֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר־ הַזֶּה֙ אַל־ הָאִ֤ישׁ בָּ֞א בֵּיתִ֔י אַֽל־ תַּעֲשׂ֖וּ אֶת־ הַזֹּֽאת׃ הַנְּבָלָ֥ה
verses.transliteration: hā·’îš ba·‘al hab·ba·yiṯ way·yê·ṣê ’ă·lê·hem way·yō·mer ’ă·lê·hem ’al- ’a·ḥay ’al- tā·rê·‘ū nā ’a·ḥă·rê ’ă·šer- haz·zeh ’al- hā·’îš bā bē·ṯī ’al- ta·‘ă·śū ’eṯ- haz·zōṯ han·nə·ḇā·lāh
verses.literal: vvv The owner of the house went out - and said to them No my brothers do not do this wicked thing . . . After all - this . . . man is a guest in my house Do not commit - this outrage

verses.original: הִנֵּה֩ אוֹצִֽיאָה־ הַבְּתוּלָ֜ה בִתִּ֨י וּפִֽילַגְשֵׁ֗הוּ נָּ֤א אוֹתָם֙ וְעַנּ֣וּ אוֹתָ֔ם וַעֲשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֑ם לֹ֣א תַעֲשׂ֔וּ הַזֹּֽאת׃ הַנְּבָלָ֥ה דְּבַ֖ר הַזֶּה֙ וְלָאִ֤ישׁ
verses.transliteration: hin·nêh ’ō·w·ṣî·’āh- hab·bə·ṯū·lāh ḇit·tî ū·p̄î·laḡ·šê·hū nā ’ō·w·ṯām wə·‘an·nū ’ō·w·ṯām wa·‘ă·śū lā·hem haṭ·ṭō·wḇ bə·‘ê·nê·ḵem lō ṯa·‘ă·śū haz·zōṯ han·nə·ḇā·lāh də·ḇar haz·zeh wə·lā·’îš
verses.literal: Look let me bring out my virgin daughter and the man’s concubine - - and you can use them and do with them as you wish - But do not do such a vile thing to this man

verses.original: הָאִישׁ֙ אָב֤וּ הָאֲנָשִׁים֙ וְלֹֽא־ לִשְׁמֹ֣עַֽ ל֔וֹ וַיַּחֲזֵ֤ק בְּפִ֣ילַגְשׁ֔וֹ וַיֹּצֵ֥א הַח֑וּץ אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וַיֵּדְע֣וּ א֠וֹתָהּ וַיִּֽתְעַלְּלוּ־ בָ֤הּ כָּל־ הַלַּ֙יְלָה֙ עַד־ הַבֹּ֔קֶר בַּעֲלוֹת הַשָּֽׁחַר׃ וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֖וּהָ
verses.transliteration: hā·’îš ’ā·ḇū hā·’ă·nā·šîm wə·lō- liš·mō·a‘ lōw way·ya·ḥă·zêq bə·p̄î·laḡ·šōw way·yō·ṣê ha·ḥūṣ ’ă·lê·hem way·yê·ḏə·‘ū ’ō·w·ṯāh way·yiṯ·‘al·lə·lū- ḇāh kāl- hal·lay·lāh ‘aḏ- hab·bō·qer ba·ʿă·lōṯ haš·šā·ḥar way·šal·lə·ḥū·hā
verses.literal: But the men would . . . not listen to him So [the Levite] took his concubine and sent her outside to them and they raped her and abused her throughout the night - - and at dawn . . . they let her go

verses.original: לִפְנ֣וֹת הַבֹּ֑קֶר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתָּבֹ֥א בֵּית־ הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ אֲדוֹנֶ֥יהָ וַתִּפֹּ֞ל פֶּ֧תַח עַד־ הָאֽוֹר׃ שָּׁ֖ם
verses.transliteration: lip̄·nō·wṯ hab·bō·qer hā·’iš·šāh wat·tā·ḇō bêṯ- hā·’îš ’ă·šer- ’ă·ḏō·w·ne·hā wat·tip·pōl pe·ṯaḥ ‘aḏ- hā·’ō·wr šām
verses.literal: Early that morning . . . the woman went back to the house - where her master was staying collapsed at the doorway and lay there until it was light . . .

verses.original: בַּבֹּ֗קֶר אֲדֹנֶ֜יהָ וַיָּ֨קָם וַיִּפְתַּח֙ דַּלְת֣וֹת הַבַּ֔יִת וַיֵּצֵ֖א לָלֶ֣כֶת לְדַרְכּ֑וֹ וְהִנֵּ֧ה הָאִשָּׁ֣ה פִֽילַגְשׁ֗וֹ נֹפֶ֙לֶת֙ פֶּ֣תַח הַבַּ֔יִת וְיָדֶ֖יהָ עַל־ הַסַּֽף׃
verses.transliteration: bab·bō·qer ’ă·ḏō·ne·hā way·yā·qām way·yip̄·taḥ dal·ṯō·wṯ hab·ba·yiṯ way·yê·ṣê lā·le·ḵeṯ lə·ḏar·kōw wə·hin·nêh hā·’iš·šāh p̄î·laḡ·šōw nō·p̄e·leṯ pe·ṯaḥ hab·ba·yiṯ wə·yā·ḏe·hā ‘al- has·sap̄
verses.literal: In the morning when her master got up and opened the doors of the house to go out . . . on his journey there was vvv his concubine collapsed in the doorway of the house with her hands on the threshold

verses.original: ק֥וּמִי וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלֶ֛יהָ וְנֵלֵ֖כָה וְאֵ֣ין עֹנֶ֑ה הָאִ֔ישׁ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ וַיִּקָּחֶ֙הָ֙ עַֽל־ הַחֲמ֔וֹר וַיָּ֣קָם לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: qū·mî way·yō·mer ’ê·le·hā wə·nê·lê·ḵāh wə·’ên ‘ō·neh hā·’îš way·yê·leḵ way·yiq·qā·ḥe·hā ‘al- ha·ḥă·mō·wr way·yā·qām lim·qō·mōw
verses.literal: Get up he told her . . . Let us go But there was no response So the man . . . put her on his donkey and set out for home

verses.original: וַיָּבֹ֣א אֶל־ בֵּית֗וֹ וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־ הַֽמַּאֲכֶ֙לֶת֙ וַיַּחֲזֵ֣ק בְּפִֽילַגְשׁ֔וֹ וַֽיְנַתְּחֶ֙הָ֙ לַעֲצָמֶ֔יהָ לִשְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר נְתָחִ֑ים וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֶ֔הָ בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֥וּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ḇō ’el- bê·ṯōw way·yiq·qaḥ ’eṯ- ham·ma·’ă·ḵe·leṯ way·ya·ḥă·zêq bə·p̄î·laḡ·šōw way·nat·tə·ḥe·hā la·‘ă·ṣā·me·hā liš·nêm ‘ā·śār nə·ṯā·ḥîm way·šal·lə·ḥe·hā bə·ḵōl gə·ḇūl yiś·rā·’êl
verses.literal: When he reached . . . his house he picked up - a knife took hold of his concubine cut her limb by limb into twelve . . . pieces and sent her throughout the territory of Israel

verses.original: וְהָיָ֣ה כָל־ הָרֹאֶ֗ה וְאָמַר֙ לֹֽא־ כָּזֹ֔את נִרְאֲתָה֙ נִהְיְתָ֤ה וְלֹֽא־ לְמִיּ֞וֹם בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עֲל֤וֹת מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם עַ֖ד הַזֶּ֑ה הַיּ֣וֹם שִֽׂימוּ־ לָכֶ֥ם עָלֶ֖יהָ עֻ֥צוּ וְדַבֵּֽרוּ׃פ
verses.transliteration: wə·hā·yāh ḵāl hā·rō·’eh wə·’ā·mar lō- kā·zōṯ nir·’ă·ṯāh nih·yə·ṯāh wə·lō- lə·mî·yō·wm bə·nê- yiś·rā·’êl ‘ă·lō·wṯ mê·’e·reṣ miṣ·ra·yim ‘aḏ haz·zeh hay·yō·wm śî·mū- lā·ḵem ‘ā·le·hā ‘u·ṣū wə·ḏab·bê·rū
verses.literal: And everyone who saw it said Nothing like this has been seen or done - from the day the Israelites . . . came out of the land of Egypt until this day Think it over . . . . . . take counsel and speak up
